instruction: Commit all changes in the current project with message 'initial commit', create an annotated tag 'v1.0' with message 'first release', and push both the commit and tag to origin.

command: git config --global user.name "xlang" && git config --global user.email "xlang2024anonym@gmail.com" && mkdir -p /home/user/projects/remote_project && cd /home/user/projects/remote_project && git init --initial-branch=main && git config receive.denyCurrentBranch ignore
unzip -q /home/user/Downloads/binder.zip -d /home/user/projects/ && cd /home/user/projects/binder && git init --initial-branch main && git remote add origin /home/user/projects/remote_project

cd /home/user/projects/remote_project; git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{for (i=2; i<=NF; i++) {printf "%s%s", $i, (i==NF ? "" : " ")}; print ""}'; git tag 2>/dev/null; tag_type=$(git cat-file -t v1.0 2>/dev/null); if [ "$tag_type" = "tag" ]; then echo "annotated_tag_verified"; else echo "not_annotated_tag"; fi; git for-each-ref refs/tags/v1.0 --format='%(contents)' 2>/dev/null; cd /home/user/projects/binder; local_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); cd /home/user/projects/remote_project; remote_id=$(git log --oneline | head -n 1 | awk '{print $1}'); if [ "${local_id}" = "${remote_id}" ]; then echo "repo is synchronous"; else echo "repo is not synchronous"; fi

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully ran git status, git add ., git commit -m 'daily update', and git push origin main in terminal. All changes pushed to remote successfully.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use terminal, run git commands (status, add, commit, push), navigate git workflow fluently
metadata.task_rationale: Tests git tagging and pushing tags in addition to commits, extending the proven push workflow with tag management
metadata.explanation: Task requires committing all files, creating an annotated tag with message 'first release', and pushing both commit and tag to origin. Evaluator checks: 1) commit message contains 'initial commit', 2) tag 'v1.0' exists on remote, 3) tag is annotated (git cat-file -t returns 'tag'), 4) tag message contains 'first release' (via git for-each-ref), 5) repos are synchronized. [Fixed: added annotated tag type verification via git cat-file -t and tag message verification via git for-each-ref]
fix_history: Fix 1: Added git cat-file -t v1.0 check with conditional marker 'annotated_tag_verified' to verify tag is annotated (not lightweight)
Fix 2: Added git for-each-ref refs/tags/v1.0 --format='%(contents)' to extract and verify tag message contains 'first release'
Fix 3: Added 'annotated_tag_verified' and 'first release' to include list, added 'not_annotated_tag' to exclude list

llm_judge_reasons: Commit message verification is correct: extracts latest commit message from remote repo via 'git log --oneline' and checks it contains 'initial commit'.
Tag presence on remote is correctly verified: 'git tag' output includes 'v1.0', confirming the tag was pushed to origin.

Annotated tag verification is correct: 'git cat-file -t v1.0' returns 'tag' for annotated tags (vs 'commit' for lightweight), and the conditional prints 'annotated_tag_verified' which is in the include list, while 'not_annotated_tag' is in the exclude list.
Tag message verification is correct: 'git for-each-ref refs/tags/v1.0 --format=%(contents)' extracts the tag annotation message, and 'first release' is checked via the include list.
Push synchronization is correctly verified: compares first commit hash between local (binder) and remote (remote_project) repos, outputting 'repo is synchronous' or 'repo is not synchronous'.
All five instruction requirements are covered: (1) commit with message, (2) annotated tag creation, (3) tag message, (4) push commit, (5) push tag.
Minor note: sync check only compares the latest commit hash, not full history, but this is sufficient for a single 'initial commit' scenario.
